services.title: Title Insurance
services.summary: Owner's and lender's policies on Texas property.
services.text: Title insurance protects you and your lender from financial loss due to defects in the property's title, such as undiscovered liens, errors in public records, or ownership disputes.
services.lead: When you buy a home, you need to be sure the seller is the true owner of the property, and that no outstanding issues damaging title transfer to you. Problems with the title can restrict the use of the property and ultimately result in financial loss. That is where title insurance comes in and where Carta Title Company, LLC can help you.
services.imageAlt: A closing file and a model house on a desk during a signing

covers.title: Owner's policy
covers.text: Protects your ownership rights, and lasts as long as you or your heirs own the property with no changes on title.

covers.title: Lender's policy
covers.text: Protects the mortgage lender's interest in the property, and ends when the loan is paid off.

covers.title: Paid once
covers.text: The cost is minimal and is only paid once. There are no renewal premiums and no expiration date on the policy.

covers.title: Rates set by the state
covers.text: In Texas, title insurance rates are fixed and regulated by the state of Texas.

questions.a: Even with a thorough title search, hidden issues can arise later. Title insurance gives you peace of mind that you're protected from covered claims.

It depends on local custom or contract negotiation. In some areas the buyer pays; in others the seller does. Generally, the seller pays for the title insurance as it guarantees no title defects for the benefit of the buyer.

questions.q: Can title insurance be transferred to a new owner?
questions.a: No, title insurance is not transferable. Each new buyer typically needs a new policy.

questions.q: Can I shop for title insurance?
questions.a: Yes, buyers have the right to choose their title company or closing agent.

faqs.q: What is a title company and what do you do?
faqs.a: A title company verifies property ownership, identifies any liens or issues, facilitates the closing process, and issues title insurance to protect both buyer and lender from potential title defects.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a title company and a real estate attorney?
faqs.a: A title company handles the research, insurance, and closing logistics, while an attorney may provide legal advice or representation on a matter, but cannot offer title insurance. A title company is licensed and regulated by the state of Texas to handle and conduct closings.

faqs.q: What fees are associated with title and closing services?
faqs.a: Typical fees include title search, settlement and escrow fees, recording fees, and title insurance premiums.
In Texas, title insurance rates are fixed and regulated by the state of Texas.

faqs.q: What is wire fraud in real estate?
faqs.a: Criminals sometimes attempt to trick buyers or agents into wiring funds to fraudulent accounts by impersonating title or escrow agents.

faqs.q: How do you protect against wire fraud?
faqs.a: We use verified communication channels, secure applications, encryption, and verbal confirmation protocols to ensure funds are securely transferred.

faqs.q: Can a title company help with a 1031 exchange?
faqs.a: Yes. While Carta Title Company doesn't serve as the Qualified Intermediary, we work closely with Equicap 1031 Exchange to ensure proper handling of exchange funds and documentation.

faqs.q: Do you offer bilingual or multilingual services?
faqs.a: Yes, we offer assistance in multiple languages to ensure a smooth experience for all clients.

faqs.q: When will I get my check from the title company?
faqs.a: We make every effort to pay all of the parties involved quickly, often the same day the transaction closes, though that varies with the day and the time of day the closing happens. Net proceeds on a sale and a Realtor's commission are usually cut the same or the next business day; if you are out of town the check is mailed, so allow an extra day or two. A Monday to Thursday closing date is a good idea if you want the funds quickly.

faqs.q: Is a wire transfer faster than a paper check?
faqs.a: Not always. Wire transfers sometimes require more verification and approvals because of cyber fraud, and as a result may even take an extra 24 hours.

facts.heading: Avoiding wire fraud
items: Always question emails that contain wiring instructions.
Always call before sending any money, and verify with the title company and your bank.
Always call after sending money to confirm the correct recipient received it.
Act immediately if anything seems unusual. Contact your bank, mortgage company and title company, and if something is wrong you may need to contact your local FBI office.

facts.heading: How the money gets stolen
facts.text: Hackers get access to the email account of someone involved in the transaction, then email that person to change the wiring instructions without the knowledge of the other parties. If it is not questioned, the wrong account receives the funds, and by closing day the money is often long gone.
